examples.nepali: समयमा आउन नसक्ने अवस्थामा, सम्पर्क गर्नुहोस् ।

examples.japanese: おかねが ひつような ばあいは、わたしに いって ください。
examples.romaji: Okane ga hitsuyō na baai wa, watashi ni itte kudasai.
examples.english: If you need money, please tell me.

examples.japanese: かじの ばあいは、しょうぼうしゃを よんで ください。
examples.romaji: Kaji no baai wa, shōbōsha o yonde kudasai.
examples.english: In case of a fire, please call a fire truck.

grammar_point: Verb/い-adj/な-adj/Noun plain form + のに、～ (even though)
form: Plain form(だ→な) + のに、～
english_explanation: Used when the result in the second half is different from what was expected.
nepali_explanation: पछिल्लो भागमा अपेक्षा गरेको भन्दा भिन्न परिणाम आएको छ भने यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: やくそくしたのに、かのじょは きませんでした。
examples.romaji: Yakusoku shita noni, kanojo wa kimasen deshita.
examples.english: Even though we had promised, she didn't come.

examples.japanese: この うちは おおきいのに、やすい です。
examples.romaji: Kono uchi wa ōkii noni, yasui desu.
examples.english: Even though this house is big, it's cheap.
examples.nepali: यो घर ठुलो भएता पनि सस्तो छ ।

examples.japanese: どようびなのに、がっこうへ いかなければ なりません。
examples.romaji: Doyōbi na noni, gakkō e ikanakereba narimasen.
examples.english: Even though it's Saturday, I have to go to school.
examples.nepali: शनिबार भएता पनि विद्यालय नगई हुँदैन ।

grammar_point: Verb (root form) ところ です。 (about to)
form: V root + ところです
english_explanation: Used to express that an action is about to begin or is at the right moment to start. Words like これから、[ちょうど]いまから make the sentence clearer.
nepali_explanation: कुनै कार्य सुरु हुन लागेको वा गर्न ठीक परेको आशय व्यक्त गर्नुपर्दा यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: これから てがみを かく ところです。
examples.romaji: Korekara tegami o kaku tokoro desu.
examples.english: I'm about to write a letter now.

examples.japanese: いまから でんわを する ところです。
examples.romaji: Ima kara denwa o suru tokoro desu.
examples.english: I'm about to make a phone call now.

grammar_point: V ている ところ です。 (in the middle of doing)
form: V ている + ところです
english_explanation: Used to express that an action is currently happening or being done. Often paired with いま.
nepali_explanation: कुनै कार्य अहिले भईरहेको वा गरीरहेको आशय व्यक्त गर्नुपर्दा यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: いま ごはんを たべて いる ところです。
examples.romaji: Ima gohan o tabete iru tokoro desu.
examples.english: I'm in the middle of eating right now.

examples.japanese: いま けっかを しらべて いる ところです。
examples.romaji: Ima kekka o shirabete iru tokoro desu.
examples.english: I'm currently checking the results.

grammar_point: V た ところ です。 (just finished)
form: V た + ところです
english_explanation: Used to indicate that an action or event has just been completed. Often paired with たったいま.
nepali_explanation: कुनै पनि कार्य भर्खर सकिएको वा पुरा भएको अवस्थालाई जनाउनको लागि यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ । त्यसैले たったいま सँग प्राय: प्रयोग हुन्छ ।

examples.japanese: たったいま ぎんこうに ついた ところ です。
examples.romaji: Tatta ima ginkō ni tsuita tokoro desu.
examples.english: I just arrived at the bank.

examples.japanese: なやんで いる ところじゃないんだよ。
examples.romaji: Nayande iru tokoro ja nai n da yo.
examples.english: This isn't the time to be worrying.

grammar_point: V た ばかり です。 (just did)
form: V た + ばかりです
english_explanation: Used to indicate that an action or event happened just a short while ago, not long ago. ばかり means 'just/recently'.
nepali_explanation: यस्ले कुनै कार्य वा घटना भएको धेरै समय वितिसकेको छैन, एकैछिन अगाडी भएको हो भनेर भन्नको लागी यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: さっき たばこを すった ばかり です。
examples.romaji: Sakki tabako o sutta bakari desu.
examples.english: I just smoked a cigarette a while ago.

examples.japanese: さっき ごはんを たべた ばかりなのに また ラーメンを たべたくなりました。
examples.romaji: Sakki gohan o tabeta bakari na noni mata rāmen o tabetaku narimashita.
examples.english: Even though I just ate a while ago, I wanted to eat ramen again.
examples.nepali: अघि भर्खर खाना खाएता पनि फेरी चाउचाउ खात मन लाग्यो ।

grammar_point: V root／V ない／い-adj／な-adj／Noun の + はず です (should/must be)
form: Various form + はず です
english_explanation: Used when the speaker is convinced that something they have guessed, thought, or reasoned is true. The scale of certainty is: はずだ > でしょう > とおもう > かもしれない.
nepali_explanation: आफ्नो अन्दाजले, बिचारले, मनले, सोचले उल्लेख गरिएको कुरा साच्चीकै हुन्छ भन्ने विश्वस्त (convinced) भएको अवस्थामा यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: ソニアさんは きょう くる はずです。けさ はなしましたから。
examples.romaji: Sonia-san wa kyō kuru hazu desu. Kesa hanashimashita kara.
examples.english: Sonia should come today, since we talked this morning.
examples.nepali: सोनियाजी आज आउनुहुनेछ । आज बिहान गफ गरेको हुनाले ।

grammar_point: Plain Form + そう です (hearsay)
form: Plain form + そう です
english_explanation: Used to pass along information received from a source without adding one's own view. If the source is stated, it is marked with ～に よると ('according to ~') at the start of the sentence.
nepali_explanation: कुनै स्रोतबाट प्राप्त गरिएको जानकारी मा आफ्नो कुनैपनि दृष्टीकोण थपनगरि व्यक्त गर्नकोलागी यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: Bhutan は とても きれいだそうです。
examples.romaji: Bhutan wa totemo kirei da sō desu.
examples.english: I've heard that Bhutan is very beautiful.
examples.nepali: मैले सुनेको भुटान असाध्यै सुन्दर छ रे ।

examples.japanese: てんきよほうに よると、あしたは すずしくなるそうです。
examples.romaji: Tenki yohō ni yoru to, ashita wa suzushiku naru sō desu.
examples.english: According to the weather forecast, it will get cool tomorrow.
examples.nepali: मौसम जानकारीको अनुसार भोली शितल हुन्छ रे ।

examples.japanese: この ケーキは おいしいそうです。
examples.romaji: Kono kēki wa oishii sō desu.
examples.english: I've heard this cake is delicious.
examples.nepali: मैले सुनेको यो केक मिठो छ रे ।

grammar_point: Verb/い-adj/な-adj/Noun plain form + ようです (appears/seems)
form: Plain form(だ→な for な-adj, だ→の for Noun) + ようです
english_explanation: Used to express an inference based on information obtained through the speaker's own senses. When ようです is combined with どうも, the speaker is not fully certain that what they say is true.
nepali_explanation: वक्ताले संवेदी अंगहरु (sensory organs) मार्फत प्राप्त गरेको जानकारीको अनुसार अनुमान व्यक्त गर्नुपर्दा यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: そとは さむいようです。
examples.romaji: Soto wa samui yō desu.
examples.english: It seems cold outside.

examples.japanese: あめが ふって いるようです。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futte iru yō desu.
examples.english: It seems to be raining.

examples.japanese: せきも でるし、あたまも いたい。どうも かぜを ひいたようだ。
examples.romaji: Seki mo deru shi, atama mo itai. Dōmo kaze o hiita yō da.
examples.english: I'm coughing and my head aches. It seems like I've caught a cold.
examples.nepali: खोकी पनि छ, टाउको पनि दुखेको छ । लाग्छ की चीसो लागेको जस्तो छ ।

grammar_point: ～そうです vs ～ようです (source of judgement)
form: Comparison
english_explanation: ①こわそうです is a judgment based on how something looks (e.g. appearance). ②こわいようです is a judgment based on something read, heard, or told by someone else.
nepali_explanation: ① मा देखाईएको आधारमा निर्णय गरीएको छ भने, ② मा चाँही व्यक्ताले कतै पढेको, सुनेको र कसैले भनिदिएको आधारमा निर्णय गरिएको छ ।

examples.japanese: トランプさんは こわそうです。
examples.romaji: Toranpu-san wa kowasō desu.
examples.english: Mr. Trump looks scary. (judged by appearance)

examples.japanese: トランプさんは こわいようです。
examples.romaji: Toranpu-san wa kowai yō desu.
examples.english: I hear Mr. Trump is scary. (judged from hearsay)

grammar_point: こえ／おと／におい／あじ が します。 (senses)
form: こえ／おと／におい／あじ が します
english_explanation: Used to express what is perceived through the senses (voice/sound/smell/taste), with the sense of being perceived without any deliberate effort or intention.
nepali_explanation: इन्द्रियहरुले बुफ्न सक्ने घटना अथवा कार्य लाई ～が します प्रयोग गरि व्यक्त गर्न सकिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: へんな おとが しますね。
examples.romaji: Hen na oto ga shimasu ne.
examples.english: What a strange sound, isn't it!

examples.japanese: なにか くさっている においが しますね。
examples.romaji: Nanika kusatte iru nioi ga shimasu ne.
examples.english: There's a smell of something rotting, isn't there!

examples.japanese: へんな あじが しています。
examples.romaji: Hen na aji ga shite imasu.
examples.english: It has a strange taste!

grammar_point: しえきどうし (Causative Verb)
form: Group I: い→あ+せます; Group II: drop ます+させます; Group III: irregular
english_explanation: Used to make someone do something or let someone do something. All causative verbs conjugate as Group II verbs.
nepali_explanation: कसैलाई कुनै कार्य गर्नलागाउन वा गराउन पर्दा Causative Verb को प्रयोग गरिनछ ।

examples.japanese: いいます → いわせます
examples.romaji: iimasu → iwasemasu
examples.english: say → make (someone) say

examples.japanese: たべます → たべさせます
examples.romaji: tabemasu → tabesasemasu
examples.english: eat → make (someone) eat

grammar_point: N(person-junior)を V (Intransitive Causative Verb)
form: N を Causative Verb (intransitive)
english_explanation: Used when a person of higher status makes a person of lower status do something. Note: if the sentence also has N(place)を with an intransitive verb, the junior person is marked with に instead.
nepali_explanation: ठुला मान्छेले साना मान्छेलाई कुनै कार्य गर्न लगाउने अवस्थामा यो स्वरुपको प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: ラムさんは ニマさんを みせへ いかせました。
examples.romaji: Ramu-san wa Nima-san o mise e ikasemashita.
examples.english: Mr. Ram made Nima go to the shop.

examples.japanese: わたしは むすめを じゆうに あそばせました。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa musume o jiyū ni asobasemashita.
examples.english: I let my daughter play freely.

examples.japanese: わたしは こどもに みちの みぎがわを あるかせます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa kodomo ni michi no migigawa o arukasemasu.
examples.english: I make the child walk on the right side of the road.
examples.nepali: म बच्चालाई बाटोको दाहिने पट्टी हिडाउछु ।

grammar_point: (superior)は N(junior)に V (Transitive Causative Verb)
form: は N に Causative Verb (transitive)
english_explanation: Used when someone of higher status makes someone of lower status do something (obligating) or permits them to do something. Even feeling-related verbs (あんしんします、しんぱいします、がっかりします、よろこびます、かなしみます、おこります) can express the junior person's expression this way.
nepali_explanation: ठुला मान्छेहरुबाट अह्राउने काम हुने भएकोले कुनै कुरालाई बाध्यत गराउँदा अथवा अनुमति दिँदा प्रयोग हुन्छ ।

examples.japanese: せんせいは せいとに じゆうに いけんを いわせました。
examples.romaji: Sensei wa seito ni jiyū ni iken o iwasemashita.
examples.english: The teacher had the students say their opinions freely.

examples.japanese: むすめに りょうりを てつだわせました。
examples.romaji: Musume ni ryōri o tetsudawasemashita.
examples.english: I had my daughter help with cooking.

examples.japanese: さくや れんらくを しなかったので、ははを しんぱいさせました。
examples.romaji: Sakuya renraku o shinakatta node, haha o shinpai sasemashita.
examples.english: Because I didn't contact her last night, I made my mother worried.
examples.nepali: हिजोरात्री सम्पर्क नगरेकोले, आमालाई चिन्तीत गराए ।

grammar_point: Causative V て いただけませんか (asking permission)
form: Causative V て-form + いただけませんか
english_explanation: In Lesson 26, V て いただけませんか was used to request someone do something; here Causative V て いただけませんか is used to ask permission for oneself to do something.
nepali_explanation: Lesson 26 मा V て いただけませんか ले कसैलाई केहीगर्न अनुरोधगर्दा प्रयोग गरिन्थ्यो भने, यस पाठमा Causative V て いただけませんか ले अनुमती माग्ने कार्यको लागी प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: あした やすませて いただけませんか。
examples.romaji: Ashita yasumasete itadakemasen ka.
examples.english: Would you please let me take tomorrow off?
examples.nepali: कृपया भोली बिदा दिनु हुन्छ की ?

examples.japanese: ここは しずか ですから、えを かかせて いただけませんか。
examples.romaji: Koko wa shizuka desu kara, e o kakasete itadakemasen ka.
examples.english: Since it's quiet here, could you let me draw a picture?
examples.nepali: यहाँ शान्त भएकोले, कृपया चित्र बनाउन दिनु हुन्छ की ?

grammar_point: けいご (honorific expressions) — overview
form: N/A
english_explanation: けいご expresses respect toward others. It reflects the relationship between speaker and listener, and the person being discussed. Three points to consider: (1) show respect to seniors/superiors; (2) show respect to strangers and people met for the first time; (3) consider the ウチ (in-group, e.g. family/company) vs. ソト (out-group) relationship — けいご is not used when speaking to outsiders about one's own in-group members. There are three types: そうけいご (respectful expressions), けんじょうご (humble expressions), and ていねいご (polite expressions).
nepali_explanation: けいご एउटा अरुप्रति गरिने आदरको अभिव्यक्ती हो । वक्ता (बोल्ने मान्छे) ले श्रोता (सुन्ने मान्छे) सँग भएको सम्बन्ध र जसको बारेमा कुरा गरिन्छ, उसंग गरिने सम्मानलाई けいご ले प्रष्ट पार्दछ ।

examples.japanese: そうけいご／けんじょうご／ていねいご
examples.romaji: sōkeigo / kenjōgo / teineigo
examples.english: respectful expressions / humble expressions / polite expressions
examples.nepali: सम्मानित अभिव्यक्ती / विनम्र अभिव्यक्ती / नम्र वा औपचारिक अभिव्यक्ती

grammar_point: そうけいご (respectful expressions) — verb conversion
form: Group I/II: as passive form; お+V ます+に なります; special respectful verbs
english_explanation: All passive-voice verb forms can also be used as respectful expressions (all fall under Group II conjugation). お + V ます-stem + に なります is an even more respectful pattern (not used for Group III or one-syllable ます-stems, or verbs that already have a special respectful form). Some verbs have entirely special respectful forms, e.g. いきます/きます/います→いらっしゃいます; いいます→おっしゃいます; しっています→ごぞんじです; みます→ごらんに なります; たべます/のみます→めしあがります; します→なさいます; くれます→くださいます.
nepali_explanation: そうけいご निकै मान दिनुपर्ने व्यक्तीहरुसंग बोलिने अभिव्यक्ती हो । अरुलाई निकै उच्चादर गरेर बोल्नुपर्दा そうけいご को प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: おとうさんは なんの しごとを されていますか。
examples.romaji: Otōsan wa nan no shigoto o sarete imasu ka.
examples.english: What kind of work does your father do?
examples.nepali: तपाईंको बावा के पेशा गर्दै होइल्सिन्छ ?

examples.japanese: ソニアさんは もう かえられました。
examples.romaji: Sonia-san wa mō kaeraremashita.
examples.english: Ms. Sonia has already gone home.

examples.japanese: こうちょうせんせいは もう おかえりに なりました。
examples.romaji: Kōchō sensei wa mō okaeri ni narimashita.
examples.english: The principal has already gone home.

examples.japanese: ジョーンズせんせいは じむしょに いらっしゃいます。
examples.romaji: Jōnzu sensei wa jimusho ni irasshaimasu.
examples.english: Mr. Jones is at the office.

examples.japanese: ジョーンズせんせいは テニスを なさいますか。 いいえ、なさらないと おもいます。
examples.romaji: Jōnzu sensei wa tenisu o nasaimasu ka. Iie, nasaranai to omoimasu.
examples.english: Does Mr. Jones play tennis? No, I don't think he does.
examples.nepali: जोन्स सर टेनिस खेलिस्छिन् ? अँह, खेलिस्दैन जस्तो लाग्छ ।

examples.japanese: こちらに おすわり ください。
examples.romaji: Kochira ni osuwari kudasai.
examples.english: Please sit here.

grammar_point: お／ご + Noun/Adjective/Adverb (honorific prefix)
form: お + Japanese-origin word; ご + Chinese-origin word
english_explanation: Beyond verbs, some nouns, adjectives, and adverbs can also be made respectful by adding お or ご at the front. Generally お attaches to Japanese-origin (kunyomi) words, and ご attaches to Chinese-origin (onyomi) words, though there are exceptions.
nepali_explanation: क्रियापदको अतिरिक्त, केही नाम (noun) हरु, विशेषण (adjective) हरु र क्रियाविशेषण (adverbs) हरुलाई पनि अघि お वा ご लगाएर सम्मानित अभिव्यक्तिमा प्रयोग गर्न सकिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: おげんき／おなまえ／おしごと
examples.romaji: ogenki / onamae / oshigoto
examples.english: health / name / job (honorific)

examples.japanese: ごかぞく／ごりょこう／ごしんせつ
examples.romaji: gokazoku / goryokō / goshinsetsu
examples.english: family / trip / kindness (honorific)

grammar_point: けいご र वाक्य शैली / वाक्यमा けいご को समान स्तर
form: Plain form + respectful verb; consistent politeness level throughout sentence
english_explanation: Honorific expressions can also end in plain form, forming a plain-style sentence, used when talking to a close friend about someone while still wanting to show respect. When using respectful expressions, all words in the sentence should be kept at a consistent level of politeness.
nepali_explanation: けいご वाक्यको एक सादा रुप (plain form) संग अन्त्य हुनसक्छ, जसले वाक्यलाई सादा शैली वाक्य (plain style sentence) बनाउँछ । सम्मानित अभिव्यक्तीको प्रयोग गर्दा वाक्यका हरेक शब्दहरुमा ख्याल गरी समान स्तरको प्रयोग गर्न जरुरी हुन्छ ।

examples.japanese: おかあさんは うちに いらっしゃる？
examples.romaji: Okāsan wa uchi ni irassharu?
examples.english: Is your mother home?

examples.japanese: スミスさまの おくさまも ごいっしょに テニスに いかれます。
examples.romaji: Sumisu-sama no okusama mo goissho ni tenisu ni ikaremasu.
examples.english: Mr. Smith's wife is also going along to play tennis.

grammar_point: V ます → まして (～まして)
form: V ます-stem + まして
english_explanation: In very polite speech, けいご V まして is used in place of V て.
nepali_explanation: धेरैनै विनम्र हुन चाहनुहुने अवस्थामा भने V て को सट्टामा けいご、V まして को प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: ゆうべ ねつを だしまして、けさも まだ さがらないんです。
examples.romaji: Yūbe netsu o dashimashite, kesa mo mada sagaranai n desu.
examples.english: I came down with a fever last night, and it still hasn't gone down this morning.
examples.nepali: हिजो राती ज्वरो आए, अज बिहानपनी अझै कमभएको छैन ।

grammar_point: けんじょうご (Humble Expression) — overview
form: N/A
english_explanation: けんじょうご is used to show respect toward others by lowering oneself, making the listener seem higher in comparison. It should generally be used only with people of much higher status or customers; overusing it can seem mocking, so care must be taken.
nepali_explanation: वक्ताले आफुलाई अरुप्रति नम्र बनाउन आफुलाई तल खसालेर वा आफुलाई तल्लो स्तरको बनाएर श्रोता वा सुन्ने व्यक्तीलाई उ उँचो भएको आभास दिलाई आदर देखाउन けんじょうご को प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: わたくしは ソニアと もうします。
examples.romaji: Watakushi wa Sonia to mōshimasu.
examples.english: My name is Sonia.
examples.nepali: मलाई सोनिया भनिन्छ । / मेरो नाम सोनिया हो ।

grammar_point: お／ご ～します (humble 'I do')
form: お + V(ます-stem, Group I & II) + します; ご + V ます(Group III) + します
english_explanation: Used to humbly say that the speaker will do something for someone. Not used with verbs whose ます-stem is a single syllable (みます、います、きます). Group III's でんわします and やくそくします are exceptions, taking お instead of ご. Not used when no other person is involved in the action.
nepali_explanation: お + V-ます (Group I & II) + します (.....गरिदिन्छु); ご + V ます (Group III)। माथीको १ र २ मा अर्को व्यक्ती संलग्न नभएको खण्डमा प्रयोग हुँदैन ।

examples.japanese: おもそうですね。おもちしましょうか。
examples.romaji: Omosō desu ne. Omochi shimashō ka.
examples.english: That looks heavy. Shall I carry it for you?

examples.japanese: わたくしが ソニアさんに スケジュールを おしらせします。
examples.romaji: Watakushi ga Sonia-san ni sukejūru o oshirase shimasu.
examples.english: I will inform Sonia of the schedule.

examples.japanese: こんしゅうの よていを ごせつめいします。
examples.romaji: Konshū no yotei o gosetsumei shimasu.
examples.english: I will explain this week's schedule.

examples.japanese: おでんわします
examples.romaji: odenwa shimasu
examples.english: I will call (you).

grammar_point: Special Humble Verbs
form: います→おります; します→いたします; しります→ぞんじます; いきます/きます→まいります; ききます/いきます→うかがいます; いいます→もうします; あいます→あめに かかります; みます→はいけんします; たべます/のみます/もらいます→いただきます
english_explanation: Certain verbs have their own entirely special humble forms; お／ご cannot be attached to these. Used when the speaker's action involves the listener or a person of respect (a), or when it does not (b).
nepali_explanation: क) वक्ताको कार्यले सुन्ने मान्छे (श्रोता) वा आदर निर्देशित मान्छेलाई समावेश गरिएको खण्डमा; ख) वक्ताको कार्यले सुन्ने मान्छे (श्रोता) वा आदर निर्देशित मान्छेलाई समावेश नगरिएको खण्डमा प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: あした てつだいいに わたくしが うかがいます。
examples.romaji: Ashita tetsudai ni watakushi ga ukagaimasu.
examples.english: I will come to help tomorrow.

examples.japanese: せんせいの おくさまに あめに かかりました。
examples.romaji: Sensei no okusama ni ome ni kakarimashita.
examples.english: I had the honor of meeting the teacher's wife.

examples.japanese: ラリトプルから まいりました。
examples.romaji: Raritopuru kara mairimashita.
examples.english: I have come from Lalitpur.

grammar_point: ていねいご (Polite Expression)
form: あります→ございます; です→でございます; いいですか→よろしいでしょうか
english_explanation: Used to show politeness toward the listener. ございます is the polite form of あります; ～で ございます is the polite form of です; よろしいでしょうか is the polite form of いいですか.
nepali_explanation: श्रोता (सुन्ने मान्छे) लाई वक्ताको आदर देखाउन ていねいご को प्रयोग गरिन्छ ।

examples.japanese: トイレは そこの ひだりに ございます。
examples.romaji: Toire wa soko no hidari ni gozaimasu.
examples.english: The restroom is on the left over there.

examples.japanese: これは ソニアさんの ほん で ございます。
examples.romaji: Kore wa Sonia-san no hon de gozaimasu.
examples.english: This is Sonia's book.

examples.japanese: 100 えん いただいても よろしいでしょうか。
examples.romaji: Hyaku-en itadaite mo yoroshii deshō ka.
examples.english: May I receive 100 yen?
